sources.entry: Hermes Agent *(NousResearch)* — The self-improving AI agent. Builds reusable skills from experience and improves them during use, giving it a compounding learning loop. Persistent cross-session memory (SQLite + FTS5), multi-platform gateway (Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, CLI), 40+ built-in tools, and RL/trajectory-generation support via Atropos. One-line install. MIT. → Website · awe

summary.one_liner: A curated, independent directory of skills, plugins, memory providers, surfaces and bridges for Nous Research's Hermes Agent, with maturity tags and trust-boundary notes.
summary.what_it_does: This is an awesome-style list, not a runnable program. It catalogs third-party skills, plugins, memory providers, messaging surfaces, and bridges for Hermes Agent, grouped into sections such as Official Resources, Skills & Plugins (community skills, agentskills.io ecosystem, registries), Memory Providers, Tools & Utilities, Integrations & Bridges, Multi-Agent, Domain Applications, and Guides. Each entry gets a maturity tag (production, beta, or experimental) plus a short description, and some entries note licenses, credential needs, or cost. The README also gives a starter path (official quickstart, then a skills pack, then a GUI or dashboard) and a trust-boundary checklist for enabling community tools. It states that it is an independent project, not an official Nous Research one, and that featured sponsor placements are paid ads rather than security endorsements.
use_cases: Find community skills to add to a Hermes Agent install
Choose a Hermes plugin for messaging, search, or storage
Look up memory providers and deployment options for Hermes
Vet third-party agent tools before enabling them
Pick a starting skill pack or GUI for a new Hermes setup
how_to_run: Read the Where Do I Start section of the README
Install Hermes Agent from the official docs quickstart
Browse the Skills & Plugins sections and pick entries by maturity tag
Install a chosen skill with the command listed in its entry, for example: hermes skills install agentrhq/authsome/skills/authsome
notable: Every entry carries a maturity tag (production, beta, experimental) with a note to re-check the linked project before relying on it
Explicit trust-boundary guidance for community skills, plugins, MCP servers and unattended cron jobs
Covers official Nous Research repos alongside community projects, clearly separated
Lists plugins and skills across many domains, including messaging bridges, memory, cost tracking, and payments
Flags high-privilege or credential-holding tools, such as mail, calendar, and social posting
caveats: Not an official Nous Research project; entries are editorial snapshots and may be outdated
Featured placements are paid advertising, not security endorsements
Many listed tools hold credentials or spend money (x402/USDC, mailbox access), so each needs review before enabling
